topics.title: 1.2 Defining Limits and Using Limit Notation

outcomes.text: Interpret limits written in analytical notation.
Understand a limit as the real value a function approaches when its input nears a specified value.
Recognize that limits can be represented graphically, numerically, or analytically.
Represent limits using mathematically correct notation.

topics.title: 1.1 Introducing Calculus: Can Change Occur at an Instant?

outcomes.text: Interpret instantaneous change by relating it to average change over intervals containing the instant.
Recognize that average rate of change is undefined when the independent variable’s change is zero.
Use limits to understand and represent changing quantities.
Define instantaneous rate of change using a limit of average rates of change.

topics.title: 1.3 Estimating Limit Values from Graphs

outcomes.text: Identify situations where a limit fails to exist, including unbounded, oscillating, or unequal one-sided behavior.
Estimate function limits.
Use a function’s graph to estimate limits.
Recognize that graph scale can conceal important behavior near a point.
Understand that limits include one-sided limits.

topics.title: 1.4 Estimating Limit Values from Tables

outcomes.text: Use numerical data to estimate limits.

topics.title: 1.5 Determining Limits Using Algebraic Properties of Limits

outcomes.text: Find function limits using limit theorems.
Apply limit theorems to sums, differences, products, quotients, and compositions.
Determine one-sided limits analytically or graphically.

topics.title: 1.6 Determining Limits Using Algebraic Manipulation

outcomes.text: Find limits by rewriting functions equivalently or applying the squeeze theorem.
Rewrite expressions into equivalent forms when doing so helps evaluate a limit.

topics.title: 1.8 Determining Limits Using the Squeeze Theorem

subtopics.title: 1.8 Determining Limits Using the Squeeze Theorem

outcomes.text: Use the squeeze theorem to determine a function’s limit.

topics.title: 1.10 Exploring Types of Discontinuities

outcomes.text: Justify continuity conclusions at a point using the definition of continuity.
Distinguish removable, jump, and vertical-asymptote discontinuities.

topics.title: 1.11 Defining Continuity

outcomes.text: A function is continuous at a point when its value and limit there exist and agree.

topics.title: 1.12 Confirming Continuity

outcomes.text: Determine intervals on which a function is continuous.
A function is continuous throughout an interval when it is continuous at every point there.
Polynomial, rational, power, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions are continuous throughout their domains.

topics.title: 1.13 Removing Discontinuities

outcomes.text: Find input values or parameters that make a discontinuous function continuous when possible.
Remove a discontinuity by defining the function’s value to equal the existing limit.
Ensure adjoining piecewise formulas and the boundary value agree at a partition boundary.

topics.title: 1.14 Connecting Infinite Limits and Vertical Asymptotes

outcomes.text: Interpret function behavior involving infinity through limits.
Extend the limit concept to describe infinite limits.
Use limits to describe and explain asymptotic or unbounded function behavior.

topics.title: 1.15 Connecting Limits at Infinity and Horizontal Asymptotes

outcomes.text: Extend the limit concept to limits as the input approaches infinity.
Use limits at infinity to describe a function’s end behavior.
Compare functions and their rates of change using relative magnitudes expressed through limits.

topics.title: 1.16 Intermediate Value Theorem

outcomes.text: Use the Intermediate Value Theorem to explain that a continuous function takes every value between its endpoint values on a closed interval.
For a continuous function on [a,b], conclude that every value between f(a) and f(b) occurs at some c between a and b.

units.title: Unit 2: Differentiation: Definition and Fundamental Properties

topics.title: 2.1 Defining Average and Instantaneous Rates of Change at a Point

outcomes.text: Find average rates of change using appropriate difference quotients.
Difference quotients calculate a function’s average rate of change over an interval.
Express a function’s derivative as the limit of a difference quotient.
Represent instantaneous rate of change using either equivalent limiting difference-quotient definition.

topics.title: 2.2 Defining the Derivative and Derivative Notation

outcomes.text: Define the derivative function as the limit of a difference quotient, when that limit exists.
Recognize dy/dx, f′(x), and y′ as standard derivative notations.
Represent derivatives graphically, numerically, analytically, or verbally.
Determine the tangent line equation at a specified point on a curve.
Use the derivative at a point as the tangent line’s slope.

topics.title: 2.3 Estimating Derivatives

outcomes.text: Estimate derivatives from available information.
Estimate a point derivative from graphical or tabular information.
Use technology to calculate or approximate a derivative at a point.

topics.title: 2.4 Connecting Differentiability and Continuity: Determining When Derivatives Do and Do Not Exist

outcomes.text: Understand how derivative functions reveal related function behavior.
Continuity at a point does not guarantee differentiability there.
Explain the relationship between differentiability and continuity.
A function differentiable at a point must be continuous there, with its derivative defined only within its domain.

topics.title: 2.5 Applying the Power Rule

outcomes.text: Use suitable derivative rules to simplify differentiation.
Calculate derivatives of familiar functions.
Differentiate functions of the form x^r using the definition or applicable rules.

topics.title: 2.6 Derivative Rules: Constant, Sum, Difference, and Constant Multiple

subtopics.title: 2.6 Derivative Rules: Constant, Sum, Difference, and Constant Multiple

outcomes.text: Differentiate sums, differences, and constant multiples using corresponding derivative rules.
Combine the power, sum, difference, and constant-multiple rules to differentiate polynomials.

topics.title: 2.7 Derivatives of cos x, sin x, and/or e^x

outcomes.text: Apply derivative rules for sine, cosine, exponential, and logarithmic functions.
Interpret a limit as the derivative definition of a known function.
Recognize a known derivative definition to evaluate some limits.

topics.title: 2.8 The Product Rule

outcomes.text: Differentiate products and quotients of differentiable functions.
Use the product rule to differentiate products of differentiable functions.

topics.title: 2.9 The Quotient Rule

outcomes.text: Use the quotient rule to differentiate quotients of differentiable functions.

topics.title: 2.10 Finding the Derivatives of Tangent, Cotangent, Secant, and/or Cosecant Functions

subtopics.title: 2.10 Finding the Derivatives of Tangent, Cotangent, Secant, and/or Cosecant Functions

outcomes.text: Rewrite tangent, cotangent, secant, or cosecant with identities before differentiating.

units.title: Unit 3: Differentiation: Composite, Implicit, and Inverse Functions

topics.title: 3.1 The Chain Rule

outcomes.text: Find derivatives of composite differentiable functions.
Use the chain rule to differentiate composite functions.

topics.title: 3.2 Implicit Differentiation

outcomes.text: Find derivatives of functions defined implicitly.
Recognize that implicit differentiation relies on the chain rule.

topics.title: 3.3 Differentiating Inverse Functions

outcomes.text: Find derivatives of inverse functions and inverse trigonometric functions.
Use the chain rule and inverse-function definition to differentiate an inverse function when its derivative exists.

topics.title: 3.4 Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions

outcomes.text: Use inverse-function differentiation methods to find derivatives of inverse trigonometric functions.

topics.title: 3.6 Calculating Higher-Order Derivatives

outcomes.text: Determine higher-order derivatives of a function.
Repeatedly differentiate a function to obtain second and higher-order derivatives.
Recognize multiple notations used for second and higher-order derivatives.

topics.title: 4.1 Interpreting the Meaning of the Derivative in Context

outcomes.text: Interpret a derivative as an instantaneous rate of change in a given context.
A derivative represents an instantaneous rate of change relative to its independent variable.
Use derivatives to represent rate-of-change information in applied situations.
Determine derivative units by dividing the function’s units by the independent variable’s units.

topics.title: 4.2 Straight-Line Motion: Connecting Position, Velocity, and Acceleration

outcomes.text: Calculate rates of change in applied settings.
Apply derivatives to rectilinear-motion problems involving position, speed, velocity, and acceleration.

topics.title: 4.3 Rates of Change in Applied Contexts Other Than Motion

outcomes.text: Interpret rates of change in applied situations.
Use derivatives to solve applied problems involving rates of change.

topics.title: 4.4 Introduction to Related Rates

outcomes.text: Calculate related rates in applied contexts.
Use the chain rule to differentiate related variables with respect to one common independent variable.
Use product and quotient rules when differentiating all variables in a related-rates equation.

topics.title: 4.5 Solving Related Rates Problems

outcomes.text: Interpret related rates in applied situations.
Solve related-rates problems by connecting one quantity’s rate to known rates of other quantities.

topics.title: 4.6 Approximating Values of a Function Using Local Linearity and Linearization

outcomes.text: Approximate a curve’s value using its tangent-line equation.
A tangent line provides a locally linear approximation near its point of tangency.
Use nearby curve behavior to decide whether a tangent-line approximation underestimates or overestimates the function.

topics.title: 4.7 Using L’Hospital’s Rule for Determining Limits of Indeterminate Forms

outcomes.text: Determine limits that produce indeterminate forms.
Ratios approaching 0/0 or infinity/infinity produce indeterminate forms.
Evaluate 0/0 and infinity/infinity limits using L’Hospital’s Rule.

topics.title: 5.1 Using the Mean Value Theorem

outcomes.text: Use the Mean Value Theorem to justify conclusions about a function over an interval.
For a continuous, differentiable function, some interior point has instantaneous rate equal to the interval’s average rate.

topics.title: 5.2 Extreme Value Theorem, Global Versus Local Extrema, and Critical Points

outcomes.text: Use the Extreme Value Theorem to justify conclusions about functions.
A continuous function on a closed interval attains at least one minimum and one maximum.
A critical point occurs where a function’s first derivative is zero or undefined.
Local extrema occur at critical points, but critical points need not be local extrema.

topics.title: 5.3 Determining Intervals on Which a Function Is Increasing or Decreasing

subtopics.title: 5.3 Determining Intervals on Which a Function Is Increasing or Decreasing

outcomes.text: Use derivative behavior to justify conclusions about a function’s behavior.
The first derivative reveals information about a function and its increasing or decreasing intervals.

topics.title: 5.4 Using the First Derivative Test to Determine Relative (Local) Extrema

subtopics.title: 5.4 Using the First Derivative Test to Determine Relative (Local) Extrema

outcomes.text: The first derivative can locate a function’s relative extrema.

topics.title: 5.5 Using the Candidates Test to Determine Absolute (Global) Extrema

subtopics.title: 5.5 Using the Candidates Test to Determine Absolute (Global) Extrema

outcomes.text: On a closed interval, absolute extrema can occur only at critical points or endpoints.

topics.title: 5.6 Determining Concavity of Functions over Their Domains

outcomes.text: A graph is concave up or down where its derivative is increasing or decreasing, respectively.
The second derivative identifies intervals where a graph curves upward or downward.
The second derivative can help locate inflection points.

topics.title: 5.7 Using the Second Derivative Test to Determine Extrema

subtopics.title: 5.7 Using the Second Derivative Test to Determine Extrema

outcomes.text: The second derivative can classify a critical point as a relative maximum or minimum.
If a continuous function has one critical point that is a local extremum, it is also the interval’s absolute extremum.

topics.title: 5.8 Sketching Graphs of Functions and Their Derivatives

subtopics.title: 5.8 Sketching Graphs of Functions and Their Derivatives

outcomes.text: Relate important function and derivative features across graphical, numerical, and analytical representations.
Use information from the first and second derivatives to predict and explain a function’s behavior.

topics.title: 5.9 Connecting a Function, Its First Derivative, and Its Second Derivative

subtopics.title: 5.9 Connecting a Function, Its First Derivative, and Its Second Derivative

outcomes.text: Relate key graphical features of a function, its first derivative, and its second derivative.

topics.title: 5.10 Introduction to Optimization Problems

outcomes.text: Use derivatives to find minimum and maximum values in applications or function analysis.
Apply derivatives to optimize a function over a specified interval.

topics.title: 5.11 Solving Optimization Problems

outcomes.text: Interpret minimum and maximum values in applied settings.
Minimum and maximum values represent specific quantities in real-world contexts.

topics.title: 5.12 Exploring Behaviors of Implicit Relations

outcomes.text: Find critical points of implicitly defined relations.
For an implicit relation, a critical point occurs where the first derivative is zero or undefined.
Use derivative evidence to justify conclusions about implicitly defined functions.
Extend derivative applications to functions defined implicitly.
Second derivatives found implicitly may involve x, y, and the first derivative.

units.title: Unit 6: Integration and Accumulation of Change

topics.title: 6.1 Exploring Accumulations of Change

outcomes.text: Interpret areas under rate-of-change graphs as accumulated change.
The area between a rate function and the x-axis represents accumulated change.
Determine the sign of accumulated change from whether the rate is positive or negative.
Express accumulated-change units as rate units multiplied by independent-variable units.
Use geometric reasoning to calculate accumulated change in suitable cases.

topics.title: 6.2 Approximating Areas with Riemann Sums

outcomes.text: Approximate definite integrals using geometric or numerical methods.
Approximate definite integrals from graphical, numerical, analytical, or verbal function representations.
Use left, right, midpoint, or trapezoidal sums with uniform or nonuniform partitions.
Compute definite-integral approximations numerically, with or without technology.
Use function behavior to identify whether an integral approximation is an underestimate or overestimate.

topics.title: 6.3 Riemann Sums, Summation Notation, and Definite Integral Notation

outcomes.text: Interpret the limiting form of a Riemann sum as a definite integral.
Recognize that the limit of an approximating Riemann sum represents a definite integral.
Describe a Riemann sum as function values multiplied by subinterval widths and then summed.
Represent the limiting form of a Riemann sum as a definite integral.
Define a definite integral as the limit of Riemann sums as partition widths approach zero.
Convert between definite-integral notation and equivalent Riemann-sum limits.

topics.title: 6.4 The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus and Accumulation Functions

outcomes.text: Use a definite integral to define a new accumulation function.
Represent accumulation functions with definite integrals.
Differentiate an accumulation function with a variable upper limit to recover its integrand.

topics.title: 6.5 Interpreting the Behavior of Functions Involving Area

subtopics.title: 6.5 Interpreting the Behavior of Functions Involving Area

outcomes.text: Use graphical, numerical, analytical, and verbal information about an integrand to analyze its accumulation function.

topics.title: 6.6 Applying Properties of Definite Integrals

outcomes.text: Evaluate definite integrals using areas and integral properties.
Evaluate suitable definite integrals geometrically using area.
Apply constant-factor, sum, reversed-limit, and adjacent-interval integral properties.
Extend definite-integral definitions to functions with removable or jump discontinuities.

topics.title: 6.7 The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus and Definite Integrals

outcomes.text: Evaluate definite integrals analytically using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
Identify an antiderivative as a function whose derivative equals the given function.
Recognize an accumulation function as an antiderivative of its continuous integrand.
Evaluate a definite integral by subtracting antiderivative values at the endpoints.

topics.title: 6.8 Finding Antiderivatives and Indefinite Integrals: Basic Rules and Notation

outcomes.text: Find antiderivatives and indefinite integrals using derivative knowledge.
Express an indefinite integral as an antiderivative plus an arbitrary constant.
Use differentiation rules as the basis for finding antiderivatives.
Recognize that some functions lack closed-form antiderivatives.

topics.title: 6.9 Integrating Using Substitution

outcomes.text: Use substitution or algebraic rearrangement to find indefinite and definite integrals.
Use variable substitution to find antiderivatives.
Change the integration limits consistently when substituting in a definite integral.

topics.title: 6.10 Integrating Functions Using Long Division and Completing the Square

subtopics.title: 6.10 Integrating Functions Using Long Division and Completing the Square

outcomes.text: Use algebraic rearrangements such as long division or completing the square to find antiderivatives.

topics.title: 7.1 Modeling Situations with Differential Equations

outcomes.text: Interpret verbal problem statements as differential equations involving derivatives.
Recognize that differential equations connect a function of an independent variable with its derivatives.

topics.title: 7.2 Verifying Solutions for Differential Equations

outcomes.text: Verify whether proposed functions satisfy given differential equations.
Use derivatives to check whether a function solves a differential equation.
Understand that a differential equation can have infinitely many solutions.

topics.title: 7.3 Sketching Slope Fields

outcomes.text: Estimate solutions to differential equations.
Understand a slope field as a graphical display of a differential equation at selected points.
Use slope fields to infer the behavior of first-order differential-equation solutions.

topics.title: 7.4 Reasoning Using Slope Fields

outcomes.text: Recognize that differential-equation solutions can be individual functions or families of functions.

topics.title: 7.7 Finding Particular Solutions Using Initial Conditions and Separation of Variables

outcomes.text: Find particular solutions of differential equations.
Understand that an initial point selects one particular solution from a general family.
Use an accumulation integral with an initial value to construct a particular solution.
Account for possible domain restrictions on differential-equation solutions.

topics.title: 7.8 Exponential Models with Differential Equations

outcomes.text: Interpret differential equations and their variables in context.
Apply general and particular differential-equation solutions to motion and exponential growth or decay.
Model proportional growth or decay with the differential equation dy/dt = ky.
Determine general and particular solutions for contextual differential-equation problems.
Solve dy/dt = ky with an initial value using an exponential model.

topics.title: 8.1 Finding the Average Value of a Function on an Interval

subtopics.title: 8.1 Finding the Average Value of a Function on an Interval

outcomes.text: Find a function’s average value over an interval using a definite integral.
For a continuous function, calculate average value by dividing its definite integral by the interval length.

topics.title: 8.2 Connecting Position, Velocity, and Acceleration of Functions Using Integrals

subtopics.title: 8.2 Connecting Position, Velocity, and Acceleration of Functions Using Integrals

outcomes.text: Use definite integrals to determine position-related values and rates for particles moving along a line.
Integrate velocity to find displacement and speed to find total distance traveled during rectilinear motion.

topics.title: 8.3 Using Accumulation Functions and Definite Integrals in Applied Contexts

outcomes.text: Explain what a definite integral means in an accumulation setting.
Recognize that an integral-defined function accumulates a rate of change.
Use the integral of a rate over an interval to determine a quantity’s net change.
Use definite integrals to calculate net change in applied situations.
Represent accumulation and net change information with definite integrals in varied applications.

topics.title: 8.4 Finding the Area Between Curves Expressed as Functions of x

subtopics.title: 8.4 Finding the Area Between Curves Expressed as Functions of x

outcomes.text: Find planar areas using definite integrals.
Calculate the area of a plane region with a definite integral.

topics.title: 8.5 Finding the Area Between Curves Expressed as Functions of y

subtopics.title: 8.5 Finding the Area Between Curves Expressed as Functions of y

outcomes.text: Find planar region areas by integrating with respect to either x or y.

topics.title: 8.6 Finding the Area Between Curves That Intersect at More Than Two Points

subtopics.title: 8.6 Finding the Area Between Curves That Intersect at More Than Two Points

outcomes.text: Calculate complex planar areas by adding multiple integrals or integrating the absolute function difference.

topics.title: 8.7 Volumes with Cross Sections: Squares and Rectangles

subtopics.title: 8.7 Volumes with Cross Sections: Squares and Rectangles

outcomes.text: Find solid volumes from known cross sections using definite integrals.
Use square or rectangular area formulas and definite integrals to calculate solid volumes.

topics.title: 8.8 Volumes with Cross Sections: Triangles and Semicircles

subtopics.title: 8.8 Volumes with Cross Sections: Triangles and Semicircles

outcomes.text: Calculate volumes with semicircular or other geometrically specified cross sections using their area formulas and definite integrals.
Use triangular cross-section formulas and definite integrals to calculate solid volumes.

topics.title: 8.9 Volume with Disc Method: Revolving Around the x- or y-axis

subtopics.title: 8.9 Volume with Disc Method: Revolving Around the x- or y-axis

outcomes.text: Calculate volumes of revolution with definite integrals.
Use the disc method and definite integrals to find volumes revolving around the x- or y-axis.

topics.title: 8.10 Volume with Disc Method: Revolving Around Other Axes

subtopics.title: 8.10 Volume with Disc Method: Revolving Around Other Axes

outcomes.text: Use the disc method and definite integrals for revolution around any horizontal or vertical line.

topics.title: 8.11 Volume with Washer Method: Revolving Around the x- or y-axis

subtopics.title: 8.11 Volume with Washer Method: Revolving Around the x- or y-axis

outcomes.text: Use the washer method and definite integrals to find ring-shaped volumes revolving around the x- or y-axis.

topics.title: 8.12 Volume with Washer Method: Revolving Around Other Axes

subtopics.title: 8.12 Volume with Washer Method: Revolving Around Other Axes

outcomes.text: Use the washer method and definite integrals for ring-shaped solids revolving around any horizontal or vertical line.

topics.title: 10.8 Ratio Test for Convergence

outcomes.text: Use limits to determine the finite sum of infinitely many terms.
Use the ratio test to determine whether a series converges or diverges.

topics.title: 10.2 Working with Geometric Series

outcomes.text: Identify a geometric series by its constant ratio between consecutive terms.
Calculate a geometric series sum as a divided by one minus r when the absolute value of r is less than one.

topics.title: 10.1 Defining Convergent and Divergent Infinite Series

subtopics.title: 10.1 Defining Convergent and Divergent Infinite Series

outcomes.text: Define the nth partial sum as the sum of the first n terms.
Recognize that a series converges to S exactly when its partial sums approach S.

topics.title: 10.3 The nth Term Test for Divergence

subtopics.title: 10.3 The nth Term Test for Divergence

outcomes.text: Use the nth-term test to establish that a series diverges.

topics.title: 10.4 Integral Test for Convergence

outcomes.text: Use the integral test to determine whether a series converges or diverges.

topics.title: 10.5 Harmonic Series

outcomes.text: Recognize harmonic, alternating harmonic, and p-series as common numerical series.

topics.title: 10.6 Comparison Tests for Convergence

outcomes.text: Use the comparison test to determine series convergence or divergence.
Use the limit comparison test to determine series convergence or divergence.

topics.title: 10.7 Alternating Series Test for Convergence

outcomes.text: Apply the alternating series test to determine whether an alternating series converges.

topics.title: 10.9 Determining Absolute or Conditional Convergence

outcomes.text: Classify a series as absolutely convergent, conditionally convergent, or divergent.
Conclude that absolute convergence implies convergence.
Explain that rearranging an absolutely convergent series preserves its sum.

topics.title: 10.10 Alternating Series Error Bound

outcomes.text: Approximate the sum of an infinite series.
Use the alternating-series error bound to estimate a partial sum’s distance from the infinite sum.

topics.title: 10.11 Finding Taylor Polynomial Approximations of Functions

outcomes.text: Represent a function at a point using a Taylor polynomial.
Determine Taylor polynomial coefficients from derivatives evaluated at the center.
Understand that higher-degree Taylor polynomials may approach the original function on an interval.
Approximate function values with a Taylor polynomial.
Use a Taylor polynomial centered at a point to approximate nearby function values.

topics.title: 10.12 Lagrange Error Bound

outcomes.text: Determine the error bound for a Taylor polynomial approximation.
Use the Lagrange error bound to establish a maximum approximation error.
Use the alternating-series error bound for some Taylor polynomial approximations.

topics.title: 10.13 Radius and Interval of Convergence of Power Series

outcomes.text: Determine a power series’ radius and interval of convergence.
Identify a power series as a series of powers centered at a real number.
Recognize that a power series converges either at one point or throughout an interval.
Use the ratio test to find a power series’ radius of convergence.
Use the radius to find the open convergence interval, then test both endpoints.
Recognize a positive-radius power series as the Taylor series of its sum within the open interval.
Know that termwise differentiation or integration preserves a power series’ radius of convergence.

topics.title: 10.14 Finding Taylor or Maclaurin Series

outcomes.text: Represent a function as a Taylor or Maclaurin series.
Understand that a Taylor polynomial is a partial sum of the corresponding Taylor series.
Interpret Taylor and Maclaurin series.
Recognize the Maclaurin series for 1/(1−x) as a geometric series.
Use the Maclaurin series for sine, cosine, and exponential functions to build other series.

topics.title: 10.15 Representing Functions as Power Series

outcomes.text: Represent a given function as a power series.
Derive power series using known series, differentiation, integration, algebra, substitutions, or geometric-series properties.

units.title: Unit 6: Integration and Accumulation of Change

topics.title: 6.11 Integrating Using Integration by Parts

outcomes.text: Use integration by parts to find indefinite and definite integrals.
Apply integration by parts to find antiderivatives.

topics.title: 6.12 Integrating Using Linear Partial Fractions

outcomes.text: Use linear partial fractions to evaluate suitable indefinite and definite integrals.
Decompose suitable rational functions into nonrepeating linear-factor fractions before integrating.

topics.title: 6.13 Evaluating Improper Integrals

outcomes.text: Evaluate improper integrals or determine that they diverge.
Identify improper integrals by infinite limits or unbounded integrands.
Evaluate improper integrals using limits of definite integrals.

topics.title: 7.5 Approximating Solutions Using Euler’s Method

outcomes.text: Use Euler’s method to approximate a differential-equation solution or a point on its curve.

topics.title: 7.6 Finding General Solutions Using Separation of Variables

outcomes.text: Find general solutions of differential equations.
Solve certain differential equations by separating variables.
Use antidifferentiation to obtain general differential-equation solutions.

topics.title: 7.9 Logistic Models with Differential Equations

outcomes.text: Interpret logistic growth models in context.
Model logistic growth when rate depends on population size and remaining carrying capacity.
Interpret logistic differential equations and initial conditions without solving them.
Determine a logistic model’s limiting value using its equation and initial conditions.
Determine the dependent variable’s value when logistic growth is fastest.

topics.title: 8.13 The Arc Length of a Smooth, Planar Curve and Distance Traveled

subtopics.title: 8.13 The Arc Length of a Smooth, Planar Curve and Distance Traveled

outcomes.text: Find the length of a planar curve defined by a function using a definite integral.
Calculate the length of a function-defined planar curve with a definite integral.

units.title: Unit 9: Parametric Equations, Polar Coordinates, and Vector-Valued Functions

topics.title: 9.1 Defining and Differentiating Parametric Equations

outcomes.text: Find derivatives for functions defined parametrically.
Derivative methods for real-valued functions also apply to parametric functions.
For a parametric curve, find the tangent slope by dividing dy/dt by dx/dt when dx/dt is nonzero.

topics.title: 9.2 Second Derivatives of Parametric Equations

outcomes.text: Calculate a parametric curve’s second derivative by differentiating dy/dx with respect to t and dividing by dx/dt.

topics.title: 9.3 Finding Arc Lengths of Curves Given by Parametric Equations

subtopics.title: 9.3 Finding Arc Lengths of Curves Given by Parametric Equations

outcomes.text: Use a definite integral to find the length of a parametrically defined plane curve.
The length of a parametrically defined curve can be found with a definite integral.

topics.title: 9.4 Defining and Differentiating Vector-Valued Functions

outcomes.text: Find derivatives of vector-valued functions.
Derivative methods for real-valued functions extend to vector-valued functions.

topics.title: 9.5 Integrating Vector-Valued Functions

outcomes.text: Find a particular solution from a rate vector and initial conditions.
Integration methods for real-valued functions extend to parametric and vector-valued functions.

topics.title: 9.6 Solving Motion Problems Using Parametric and Vector-Valued Functions

outcomes.text: Find positions and rates of change for planar motion problems.
Use derivatives to find velocity, speed, and acceleration along parametric or vector-defined paths.
Integrating velocity gives displacement; integrating speed gives total distance traveled.

topics.title: 9.7 Defining Polar Coordinates and Differentiating in Polar Form

outcomes.text: Find derivatives of functions expressed in polar coordinates.
Derivative methods for real-valued functions extend to polar-coordinate functions.
Derivatives with respect to the polar angle provide information about a polar curve, including its first and second slopes.

topics.title: 9.8 Finding the Area of a Polar Region or the Area Bounded by a Single Polar Curve

subtopics.title: 9.8 Finding the Area of a Polar Region or the Area Bounded by a Single Polar Curve

outcomes.text: Use definite integrals to find areas of regions defined by polar curves.
The rectangular-coordinate area concept extends to regions described in polar coordinates.

topics.title: 9.9 Finding the Area of the Region Bounded by Two Polar Curves

subtopics.title: 9.9 Finding the Area of the Region Bounded by Two Polar Curves

outcomes.text: Definite integrals can calculate areas bounded by two polar curves.
